metadata.title: Arithmetic Bill
metadata.description: Compute a purchase total and its 10% GST in whole cents, printing both as dollars with 2 decimals.

instructions.main: An item costs 4999 cents ($49.99) and the customer buys 3. Compute the total, then the 10% GST, and print both as dollar amounts rounded to 2 decimals.
steps: Work in whole cents: `total_cents = price_cents * qty`.
The 10% GST in whole cents is `gst_cents = total_cents // 10` (floor division keeps money as whole cents).
Convert to dollars when printing: `Total: <value>` then `GST: <value>`, each on its own line with exactly 2 decimals (use `"{:.2f}".format(...)`).

hints.message: Set `price_cents = 4999` and `qty = 3`, compute `total_cents = price_cents * qty` and `gst_cents = total_cents // 10`, then print both in dollars with `{:.2f}`.
The GST must stay whole cents: `total_cents / 10` keeps a fraction of a cent — use floor division `total_cents // 10`.
Print money with rounding: `"{:.2f}".format(value)` rounds to 2 decimals, but `str()` prints every digit.
Your last run didn't pass — check that the total and the GST are each printed on their own line with exactly two decimals.

evaluation.feedback_on_all_pass: The total and GST are computed in cents and printed with 2 decimals.

test_cases.feedback_on_pass: Both amounts print with exactly two decimals.
test_cases.feedback_on_fail: Print the total as `Total: 149.97` and the GST as `GST: 14.99`, each on its own line with exactly two decimals.

test_cases.feedback_on_pass: You computed a product into a variable.
test_cases.feedback_on_fail: Compute the total as a product: `total_cents = price_cents * qty`.
